title: Convergent soft cutover with session heartbeat reconciliation for active-active edge
creator: Mariana Park
description: Implement a convergent soft cutover mechanism for our hosted API edge to support active-active multi-region failover while preserving session/stream continuity. The feature uses heartbeat reconciliation, ephemeral token stitching, compact KV checkpointing, and progressive traffic redistribution to minimize dropped streaming sessions and meet SLOs during cutovers and degraded conditions.
acceptance_criteria: Cutover flow can migrate 95% of active streaming sessions without full reconnect under normal load in the staging multi-region testbed.
P99 non-stream request latency increase <= 30ms during progressive 0->100% traffic shift at target RPS in staging.
Circuit breaker engages and redirects >99% of requests flagged by overload policy to fallback model variants or lower-cost region according to routing policy.
Operational runbook created and validated by oncall in a chaotic failover drill.
Console dashboards show per-route session continuity rate, stitched-token success rate, KV checkpoint freshness, and load-shedding incidents.
Security review completed for ephemeral token stitching and KMS usage.
updates: 2026-02-15: Triage — scoped problem: live sessions (streaming) are most at risk during region failovers; plan spike to explore token stitching vs full state replication.
2026-02-20: Spike complete — PoC shows token-stitching + KV checkpointing reduces reconnects by ~78% on a 1k concurrent-stream test. Evidence: github.com/redwood/edge/PR/1281 (prototype).

2026-02-25: Architecture review — chosen approach: heartbeat reconciliation + compact per-session checkpoints in region-local KV + ephemeral token stitching for handoff; trade-off: adds ~4KB metadata per active session but avoids cross-region live-state streaming.

2026-02-28: Integration plan drafted — components: cutover controller, heartbeat reconciler, stitch service, circuit-breaker policy manager, and console telemetry hooks. Design doc: confluence.redwood.ai/edge/resilience/cutover-design-2026-02-28.
2026-03-01: Resource assignment — infra to provision ephemeral KMS keys for stitch tokens; SRE to add canary-based throttle; plan end-to-end test in staging 2026-03-22.
decisions: Favor eventual session continuity (stitching) over strict synchronous KV replication to limit cross-region latency and cost.
Use a 3-stage progressive traffic spray (1%, 10%, 100%) with SLO gates (error & latency thresholds) to control cutover velocity.
Implement circuit-breaker thresholds with two levers: latency window breach (p95>200ms for 30s) and queue-depth breach (>80% of dispatch capacity).
Load-shedding policy will be token-priority aware: best-effort trimming first on non-critical routes and only shed streaming tail tokens at high contention.
Ephemeral stitch tokens expire in 60s by default and are rotated via KMS; revocation fed to gateway caches to avoid replay windows.
Telemetry: emit stitched_session_success boolean, stitch_latency_ms, kv_checkpoint_age_seconds, and load_shed_count per route.
technical_notes: Heartbeat reconciliation: each region writes lightweight heartbeats (session_id, last_offset, epoch) to regional KV; reconciler compares epoch vectors to decide stitch candidate.

Stitch flow: source region issues signed ephemeral token including session_id, last_offset, model_variant_hint; target region verifies signature via KMS and attempts in-memory KV hydration before resuming stream.
Checkpoint format: compressed protobuf with fields {session_id, last_offset, kv_digest, model_variant_hint}; aim for <4KB per active session using delta encoding.
Circuit breaker: client-facing gateway runs local fast path checks; if tripped, returns HTTP 429 with x-redwood-fallback:route header to trigger client-side fallback or server-side downgrade.
Load shedding: implement both drop-tail and probabilistic shed (p-shed) depending on route SLA; streaming routes prefer p-shed on tail tokens to preserve head-of-conversation continuity.
Observability: prebuilt Grafana dashboards for synthetic canary metrics and an alert rule that aborts cutover and rolls back if stitched_session_success < 85% and error_rate increase > 2x baseline.
qa_steps: Run multi-region staging scenario with 5k mixed sessions (1:5 streaming:short-request) and perform a 3-stage cutover.
Validate that >90% streaming sessions resume without client reconnect and that client sees consistent sequence offsets.
Introduce slow-path kernel in one region to simulate overloaded backend and verify circuit breaker redirects traffic according to routing policy.
Chaos test: kill region controller during stage 2 and confirm system converges without user-visible corruption and with acceptable SLO degradation.
Soak test for 48 hours at sustained 2x baseline traffic to validate KV checkpoint churn and cost impact.
notes_for_oncall: During staged cutovers watch stitch success and kv_checkpoint_age. Abort cutover if stitch success < 80% over a 2-minute window. Use emergency rollback flag in cutover controller to divert to original region.
